transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-21
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes (approx)
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Alex Marshall (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Clara Weiss (MediCorps), Lars Meier (MediCorps), Sofia Alvarez (MediCorps legal)

Summary: High-level security review focused on data residency and region pinning. Customer is EU-headquartered (Germany) and needs assurance that PHI-like data won't cross borders, wants RBAC/SSO assurances, KMS/key control options, and a clear list of sub-processors. Discussed hosted vs dedicated vs private deployments and fallback behaviours. Agreed next steps and action items.

Topics: data residency, region pinning, cross-border processing, sub-processors, KMS integration, audit logs, SOC2/ISO documentation, SSO/SAML, RBAC, dedicated vs private deployment tradeoffs.

Transcript body:
[00:00:12] Alex Marshall: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, hi Priya.
[00:00:18] Priya Desai: Hi all, Priya from Redwood, I'll handle the tech bits.
[00:00:22] Clara Weiss: Hi this is Clara, head of security at Medicorp — hi Lars, Sofia.
[00:00:26] Lars Meier: Hey.
[00:00:28] Sofia Alvarez: Hello.
[00:00:31] Alex Marshall: Awesome. Agenda today is region pinning and data residency: how we ensure data stays in EU for processing, what our sub-processor list looks like and KMS options. 
[00:00:45] Clara Weiss: Yes, we have pretty strict rules — anything that could be considered PHI must not leave EU borders. We also need audit logs for all user activity and encryption keys we control if possible.
[00:00:58] Priya Desai: Totally understood. At a high level Redwood supports three deployment modes — hosted, dedicated, and private. For strict residency the common choices are Redwood Dedicated with EU-only capacity, or Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) if they need customer-managed networking. 
[00:01:18] Lars Meier: Can you just clarify the difference? Dedicated is still managed by Redwood but reserved GPUs in EU, right? Private is we run it in our VPC or on-prem?
[00:01:30] Priya Desai: Correct — Dedicated = Redwood-managed nodes that are physically in EU regions (we can pin requests to those pools). Private = the control plane is in Redwood but the inference plane runs in your VPC or on-prem, customer-managed. Private gives you more control over keys and network egress. 
[00:01:48] Clara Weiss: If we do Dedicated, what guarantees do we have that a request won't be routed to US for failover? We need no cross-border processing unless explicitly approved.
[00:01:59] Alex Marshall: Great question. We have routing policies: region pinning can be configured at the tenant or route level. Default behavior for a tenant pinned to EU is to only use EU capacity. We do have fallback policies, but for Medicorp we can configure no-cross-border fallback — which means if EU capacity is exhausted requests will be throttled rather than routed to other regions.
[00:02:21] Priya Desai: To add, we also support per-request region hints and a hard pin option. Hard pin = enforce EU-only, no automatic cross-region failover. Soft pin = prefer EU first, then failover to other regions per policy. 
[00:02:35] Lars Meier: How is that enforced from an infra standpoint? Is the control plane aware of region tags and does it check before routing?
[00:02:43] Priya Desai: Yes, the control plane stores capacity tags and the routing layer enforces policy at request admission time. There's a routing decision step that considers tenant pin, model variant availability, and latency SLOs. If hard pin and no available EU capacity, the request returns 429/503 depending on config — we can surface that to your app.
[00:03:01] Clara Weiss: OK good. Next — keys. We need customer-managed encryption keys (bring-your-own-key-like) for model input at rest and S3 buckets where logs are stored. How does Redwood integrate with KMS?
[00:03:16] Priya Desai: We support KMS integrations. For Redwood Dedicated we can integrate with customer KMS through cross-account roles in cloud providers; for Private you can use your on-prem HSM or KMS inside your VPC. Currently supported patterns: AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and customer HSM via KMIP for private deployments.
[00:03:36] Sofia Alvarez: And audit logs — we need immutable logs of access and admin actions, and they must be stored in EU. Do you provide audit exports?
[00:03:46] Alex Marshall: Yes, we surface audit logs via the Console and provide S3 export of logs to a customer-owned EU bucket. We also have write-once retention policies as an add-on.
[00:03:58] Priya Desai: One caveat on exports: in Hosted mode, logs are managed by Redwood and stored in the region(s) where your tenant is pinned. If you need absolute custody we recommend Dedicated with S3 export to your account or Private.
[00:04:15] Lars Meier: Sub-processors — who is involved? We need a list because our legal team will need to run DPA and sub-processor approval.
[00:04:24] Alex Marshall: We have a standard sub-processor list that includes major cloud providers in the region (e.g., AWS EU-West, GCP Europe), monitoring providers, and storage partners. I'll attach the most recent list. We can also provide SOC2 reports for our key sub-processors.
[00:04:38] Clara Weiss: Any chance certain sub-processors are US-based and could see data?
[00:04:42] Priya Desai: For Dedicated EU-only setup we limit sub-processor usage to EU regions where possible; however some vendor control planes are global. We'll surface which ones have global control planes and provide mitigations (e.g., data plane stays in EU, control plane metadata anonymized).
[00:04:58] Lars Meier: You mentioned anonymization — can you detail what metadata might cross borders? We need to know exact fields.
[00:05:06] Priya Desai: Sure, typical control-plane metadata includes usage counters, allocation IDs, and non-PII telemetry. Model payloads and logs are kept in-region. We'll provide an itemized mapping doc.
[00:05:18] Sofia Alvarez: Please make sure that mapping is explicit — legal can't sign without it.
[00:05:22] Alex Marshall: Agreed. We'll attach the mapping.
[00:05:25] [00:05:31] Alex Marshall: Quick question on SSO: we currently use SAML 2.0 via our IdP. How is SSO handled?
[00:05:36] Priya Desai: Redwood supports SAML and OIDC. For Dedicated and Private, we can enable SCIM provisioning and enforce RBAC tied to your IdP groups. Admin actions are tied to user identity and logged.
[00:05:49] Clara Weiss: RBAC model — can we map our fine-grained roles? For example, separate the model deployment team from analytics so analytics can't exfiltrate raw requests.
[00:05:58] Priya Desai: Yes, RBAC is policy-driven; we have prebuilt roles and you can create custom roles scoped to routes (e.g., embedding-only, deploy-only). We'll show examples.
[00:06:09] Lars Meier: Is there token-level auditing — who saw which request, which user invoked what route?
[00:06:14] Priya Desai: Yes, audit logs capture token/user, route, model version, timestamp, and raw request ID. For privacy we can redact payloads in logs by configuration, but that reduces ability to debug.
[00:06:27] Clara Weiss: Redaction is fine as long as we can re-run requests in a safe sandbox for debugging.
[00:06:32] Priya Desai: We offer replay tooling in Private deployments. For Hosted/Dedicated, we can run controlled replays with your consent and under strict access controls.
[00:06:44] [00:06:50] Alex Marshall: On certification — SOC2 and ISO 27001 status?
[00:06:55] Priya Desai: Redwood has SOC2 Type II in 2024 and ISO 27001 cert — I'll attach the certs. For Dedicated/private we can provide the relevant control mapping and the auditor's report redacted copy.
[00:07:07] Sofia Alvarez: Will you provide a responsibility matrix for shared controls?
[00:07:12] Alex Marshall: Yes, we'll send a shared responsibility matrix mapping which controls are Redwood vs customer.
[00:07:16] [00:07:22] Lars Meier: One technical nit — what about model caching and KV cache — is there any key material or cached prompt history that could be stored outside the EU? We saw a note about KV cache in the docs.
[00:07:33] Priya Desai: The KV cache is part of the inference runtime; caching is in-memory on the GPU host and persisted only if enabled for warm start. For EU-only we ensure those persistence stores are in EU. We can turn off cross-region cache synchronization.
[00:07:48] Clara Weiss: Good. What about backups? Snapshot schedules?
[00:07:52] Priya Desai: Snapshots are stored per-region; for Dedicated we keep backups in EU. For Private you control backup locations.
[00:07:58] [00:08:04] Alex Marshall: Another concern often raised is cross-border logging for support triage. How do we handle support engineers needing to view logs that might be in EU?
[00:08:14] Priya Desai: Support access is audited and can be limited to EU-based staff only for your tenant. We can also require customer approval before logs are accessed — a gating workflow.
[00:08:24] Sofia Alvarez: And subprocessor changes — we need notification windows and opt-out rights if a new subprocessor is outside EU.
[00:08:33] Alex Marshall: Our DPA includes a 30-day notice window for material subprocessor changes and an approval/objection process. We'll surface specifics.
[00:08:41] [00:08:47] Lars Meier: On data residency proof — can you provide periodic attestation that data never left EU? Like a signed statement?
[00:08:55] Priya Desai: We can provide logs showing region routing decisions and signed attestations for a period. For Dedicated we can also provide a weekly exported routing audit.
[00:09:07] Clara Weiss: That's useful. Cost question — is Dedicated materially more expensive than Hosted pinned region?
[00:09:14] Alex Marshall: Dedicated carries a capacity reservation premium; it tends to be higher but gives SLAs and isolation. Hosted pinned region is a cheaper option but we can't guarantee the same capacity reservation. We can model costs in a follow-up spreadsheet.
[00:09:29] [00:09:35] Lars Meier: Latency guarantees — if we pin EU, what's the latency SLO?
[00:09:40] Priya Desai: We publish per-model performance profiles; Dedicated customers can get a latency SLA per route once we agree on sizing. We'll include sample SLOs in the doc pack.
[00:09:52] Clara Weiss: For legal — any cross-border legal exposure from sub-processors in US? We need to ensure EU data protection laws covered.
[00:09:59] Sofia Alvarez: (adds) and standard contractual clauses?
[00:10:02] Alex Marshall: We include SCCs where needed and have a DPA with EU data protection clauses. We'll share our standard DPA and SCC annex.
[00:10:10] [00:10:16] Priya Desai: Quick note about telemetry — we can configure what telemetry leaves the region. For tightest settings we only send anonymized metrics to global analytics and keep request-level telemetry in-region.
[00:10:29] Lars Meier: Ok that covers a lot. Can you also confirm physical hosting regions (e.g., eu-west-1, europe-west3) you operate in?
[00:10:36] Alex Marshall: Yes, we have EU-West (Ireland), EU-Central (Frankfurt), and multiple GCP European regions. We'll attach a region list and a mapping to our capacity pools.
[00:10:47] [00:10:53] Priya Desai: I'll also call out a few implementation notes: 1) Tenant-level hard pin flag, 2) KMS cross-account role example for AWS, 3) S3 log export IaC snippet, 4) sample RBAC policy mapping.
[00:11:08] Clara Weiss: Great. Please include those snippets — our platform team will want Terraform examples.
[00:11:13] Priya Desai: Noted.
[00:11:15] [00:11:21] Alex Marshall: Any blockers on timeline — Clara you mentioned you need legal sign-off by end of September?
[00:11:27] Clara Weiss: Yes ideally September 30th. We want to start a pilot in early October.
[00:11:31] Alex Marshall: OK we'll aim to get everything by 2025-08-25 so you have time to review.
[00:11:37] [00:11:43] Sofia Alvarez: One minor transcription glitch to flag — please ensure the control-plane metadata doc lists precise fields. Legal will push back on ambiguous terms like 'anonymized'.
[00:11:54] Alex Marshall: Understood — we'll be explicit.
[00:11:58] [00:12:04] Priya Desai: Final note on sub-processors — for any US-based control plane vendors we provide mitigations like encryption in transit with customer keys and no PII in control-plane payloads.
[00:12:18] Lars Meier: Sounds reasonable.
[00:12:20] [00:12:26] Alex Marshall: Let's do a quick recap and next steps.
[00:12:29] Priya Desai: Recap: 1) We'll send region-pinning architecture and hard/soft pin definitions. 2) KMS integration guide and IaC snippets. 3) Sub-processor list and control-plane metadata mapping. 4) SOC2/ISO and DPA + SCCs. 5) Cost/capacity modeling spreadsheet.
[00:12:47] Clara Weiss: Perfect. One more ask — can you mark support access to EU-only staff for our tenant?
[00:12:53] Alex Marshall: Yes we'll put that as a requirement in the ticket and include it in the DPA addendum.
[00:12:59] [00:13:05] Alex Marshall: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up by email with the doc pack and schedule the pilot kickoff once legal signs off.
[00:13:13] Sofia Alvarez: Thanks.
[00:13:14] Lars Meier: Thanks all.
[00:13:16] Priya Desai: Thanks, bye.
